aggregates.claim: A finite ledger over the exact current collected suite, with every execution ID, primary requirement, input/profile fingerprint, current adjudication, declared phase and evidence class bound into the inventory review. Inventory adjudication is distinct from case approval: explicit current needs-oracle or disputed members remain listed, unapproved and ineligible for qualified passes. Unreviewed, stale or falsely labelled reference evidence cannot be silently adopted. Declared-valid runtime effects, other effects, positive admission controls, undefined-result contexts and invalid-input diagnostics have separate populations. Actual observations are joined by exact ID and compiler configuration without adding an execution or attributing a canonical case to this requirement.
aggregates.limitation: Observational infrastructure only: S4.2-001's facet remains pending until the source/requirement census, complete conforming fixture/oracle inventory and separate processor/dependency qualifications are independently established. No finite run proves the universal processor obligation. A filtered invocation retains all unselected members in its denominator. XFAILs remain failures; skips, unsupported modes, missing profiles, unavailable launchers, unexecuted run effects and provisional observations cannot become qualified passes. A compile/link admission is not execution of an interpretation, and a context-only run is not an assertion about an undefined value. Resource failures do not establish permitted size/complexity limits. Compiler headers, companions, launchers and profile observations describe the selected interface, not ABI certification or universal portability. Paragraphs 7-8 are recommendations, not manufactured mandatory documentation requirements.

review.rationale: Renewal of the whole-suite execution inventory after the ASSOCIATE construct FIXTURE packet in doc/source_audits/batch_121.json, and after a corrective renewal of six catalogue source reviews described below. The member count moves from 2124 to 2134 because this packet adds ten executable cases; authored_facets moves 1829 to 1839, pending facets 5055 to 5045, and fixture review states 1811 to 1821 reference-validated with 274 source-reviewed and 1 needs-oracle unchanged. The full suite is 984 tests, OK. tests/expected_failures.txt is unchanged by this packet and stands at 807 lines after the three WHERE restoration XFAILs recorded in batch120. These are the first Clause 11 fixtures in the suite: Clause 11.1 was source-complete at 268 of 268 base units but had no executable tests at all. Ten facets are established across S11.1.3.2-001, -002 and -003 and S11.1.3.3-001 and -005. Non-vacuity was proved by mutation rather than inspection, and the central claim, that the associating entity's bounds differ from the selector's subscripts, was verified by mutating the expected bounds to the selector's subscript values and confirming failure; the reviewer independently recomputed that base with subscripts minus three to three by two has extent four and associated bounds one to four, that base with subscripts twelve to twenty by three has extent three and bounds one to three, that the rank-two strided section has shape three by two, and that the character section has length six. Mutating that length from six to the parent's nine also failed, which is the specific guard against the blank-padding trap, and every length assertion uses LEN explicitly rather than a comparison. One mutation was applied deliberately in the reverse direction: weakening the outer scoping sentinel to a value written inside the construct made the test stop discriminating, proving that the sentinel choice does real work. The inquiry intrinsics are legitimate oracles here only because the standard requires the asserted values, and each plan states that justification. The definable-selector-assignment facet is correctly classified as a positive control rather than a full effect because its owning requirement is a restriction. Twenty-three facets remain pending on unregistered Clause 15 and Clause 19 material, polymorphism, coarrays, branch ownership from unregistered 11.2, and a refusal to assume a nondefault kind exists. All ten cases pass under both the frozen LFortran 0.65.0-411-ga0afaa840b-dirty and gfortran 16.1.0 with -std=f2023, reproduced by the integrator; ASSOCIATE with strided section selectors is exactly where a compiler may be wrong, so the independently recomputed bounds and not the compiler agreement are what validate these. Separately and importantly, this renewal records a corrective action. Binding facets into a catalogue changes its content and therefore stales its content-bound source review by design. Batches 118, 119 and 120 each left such staleness uncorrected, and it was surfaced only when a linked-evidence test exercised 11.1.3.3. The source reviews for 9.5.3.3, 10.1.5.2.2, 10.1.5.3.1, 10.2.3.2, 11.1.3.2 and 11.1.3.3 have now all been renewed, each recording that the staleness is attributable solely to facet binding, that the source accounting is unchanged with no unit added, removed or redispositioned and no requirement renumbered or reused, and that the renewal carries the original independent source review forward without adding any new source claim. All remaining pending facets, unresolved units, the retained needs-oracle real-BOZ block and every global gate remain open.
